clue.text: Car Lily scuffed — it can be waxed

indicators.note: scuffed means roughed up and knocked out of shape, so the letters of car and lily are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a car belonging to Lily has been scraped, and remarks that a coat of wax will put it right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it can be waxed' looks like car polish; it refers to the idiom 'wax lyrical', to talk enthusiastically. 'scuffed' shuffles CARLILY.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'wax lyrical' means to speak with gushing enthusiasm, so this adjective is the thing one can wax.

clue.text: Advance round church, seeing small body of water

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the advance goes around church

parts.note: an advance of money is a loan

explanation.surface: Moving forward around a church, someone comes upon a little lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' looks like a verb of movement; it is a loan of money. A lochan is a small Scottish loch.
explanation.definitionFit: A lochan is a small loch or pond, Scottish Gaelic in origin, a little lake.

clue.text: Compunction concerning titbit left to go off

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: left to go off means the letter for left departs from the word

parts.note: a titbit is a morsel

explanation.surface: Someone feels guilty about leaving a tasty snack to spoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' suggests food spoiling; it means the L leaves MORSEL, giving MORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Compunction is a pang of guilt or regret, a near synonym for remorse.

clue.text: Wrinkle initially spotted in aquatic plant

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the plant name

parts.note: water crowfoot is a buttercup that grows in streams and ponds

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A wrinkle is first noticed on a water plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' looks like the verb 'noticed'; only its first letter is used. Water crowfoot is a white-flowered buttercup of ponds.
explanation.definitionFit: Crow's-feet are the fine lines spreading from the outer corner of the eye, each one a wrinkle.

clue.text: Commission a tune, nicely arranged

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, as a piece of music is arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer is commissioned to write a tune and arrange it nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commission' looks like a verb about ordering music; it is a noun, an officer's rank. 'arranged' rearranges ATUNENICELY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenancy is the rank or office of a lieutenant, held by an officer's commission in the armed forces.

clue.text: With a lot of good fortune, bird discovers edible plant

indicators.note: a lot of a word, but not all of it, means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: good fortune is luck
the erne is the sea eagle, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A lucky birdwatcher stumbles on a plant fit to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims LUCK to LUC; 'discovers' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is alfalfa, a clover-like forage crop eaten by livestock and as sprouts by people.

clue.text: The fate of one whose wife was backward-looking?

definitions.meaning: one's fate is one's destiny or portion in life
in Genesis this man's wife looked back at Sodom and was turned into a pillar of salt

explanation.walkthrough: 'backward-looking' sounds like a description of a conservative spouse but is literal: the biblical wife looked back.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's lot is their destiny; the second reading is the biblical nephew of Abraham.

clue.text: In Mexico a tireless consumer of flesh

indicators.note: In means the answer is found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In Mexico an animal tirelessly eats meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'MexiCO A TIreless'. The coati is a raccoon relative of the Americas that eats small animals as well as fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is an omnivorous mammal that eats insects, lizards and small animals, so it is a consumer of flesh.

clue.text: Dress again in large shifts

indicators.note: shifts means moves around, so the letters of in large change places

explanation.surface: Someone puts on new clothes, in large-size shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' looks like dresses, the garments; it is the anagram signal for INLARGE. To dress ranks is to line them up.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress troops is to straighten their line, so to do it again is to bring them back into alignment.

clue.text: Compromise fellow involved in green revolution

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the fellow sits within the jumbled letters
revolution means turning over, so the letters of green are rearranged

parts.note: Dan is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A man caught up in an environmental revolution puts things at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' makes ENGER from the jumbled letters. 'Compromise' is a verb here, to put at risk, not a settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise safety or security is to expose it to danger, to put it in jeopardy.

clue.text: Part of heartless remark about horse losing tail

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened remark is wrapped around the shortened horse
heartless means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a remark is a comment

indicators.note: losing its tail means the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: A cruel comment is made about a horse whose tail has been docked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves COMENT; 'losing tail' leaves PON. 'Part of' reads as a phrase, but 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A component is one constituent piece of a larger whole, a straightforward synonym for a part.

clue.text: Arbitrator's decision a disadvantage?

annotationWithheld.why: Arbitrator's decision a disadvantage? (5): AWARD only comes from 'a drawback' read as A + DRAW reversed, so 'disadvantage' would supply DRAW and also signal the reversal, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Tapestry shows Scottish island — south, not north

indicators.note: south, not north means an S stands where an N was

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland

explanation.surface: A display of tapestries features a Scottish island, with a note on which way to head.
explanation.walkthrough: The final N of ARRAN is replaced by S. ARRAS is a wall hanging, named after the French town famous for weaving.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a rich woven wall hanging, named after the French town once famous for producing such tapestries.

clue.text: General course an artist announced

indicators.note: announced means the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a course for a sailing boat is a tack, and an artist is a Titian, a work or painter like the Venetian master

explanation.surface: A military commander's battle plan is described alongside a painter, as if in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an adjective but is a military leader. Said aloud, TACK + TITIAN sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A general is a commander skilled in planning manoeuvres, someone expert in the art of battle tactics.

clue.text: Money detectives enclosed with drug? It's pure chance

parts.note: coin is money in metal form
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosed, written at the foot of a letter
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Finding cash and police officers together with drugs is just an accident, someone claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosed' looks like a container signal but is the letter-writing abbreviation ENC. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A coincidence is a chance occurrence of events that seem connected but are not.

clue.text: Preliminary survey involving study in Leonardo's time

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Leonardo da Vinci lived during the Renaissance
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: An art historian sets out to survey the period when Leonardo da Vinci worked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' as CON is an old sense, to learn by heart. 'Leonardo's time' points to the period, not a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconnaissance is a scouting exploration made before action, an initial survey of the ground.

clue.text: Utopian retreat a northern girl has developed

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new form, so these letters are remade

explanation.surface: A girl from the north has built herself a perfect hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' looks like a link word but is part of the anagram ANGIRLHAS.
explanation.definitionFit: In James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon this is a hidden Himalayan paradise, now any idyllic haven.

clue.text: Copy giving bad impression

definitions.meaning: a separately printed copy of an article from a journal
read as two words, a print that is off, not up to standard

explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' links the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: An offprint is a reproduction of one article; split as off print, it is a poor printed impression.

clue.text: Potential for success provided by Tweedledum's rattle?

definitions.meaning: a real prospect of winning if one makes the effort
in Through the Looking-Glass, Tweedledum and Tweedledee agree to have a battle over a spoilt rattle, so the rattle was their occasion for a fight

explanation.walkthrough: 'provided by' links the two readings. The second is whimsical: the rattle gave the twins an opportunity to come to blows.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a reasonable possibility of succeeding, given determined effort; the second reading takes it literally as an occasion for combat.

clue.text: Fish river during rift with president

indicators.note: during means within, so the river sits inside the rift

parts.note: a rift is a gap
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A fish lives in a river that runs through a gorge where a president once stood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. 'river' as R is a standard abbreviation; Ike was Dwight Eisenhower's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The garpike, or garfish, is a long slender fish with beak-like jaws.

clue.text: Bird sound — and another made when capturing game?

indicators.note: when capturing means holding inside, so the second bird call holds the game

parts.note: another bird sound is a chirp
RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: A bird calls, then another calls as it catches its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like hunted prey, but it is rugby union. 'made' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirrup is a short repeated chirping sound made by a bird or insect.

clue.text: A rider to be in awe of

definitions.meaning: Paul ... made a famous midnight ride in 1775 to warn of British troops
to hold someone in deep respect

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading names the American patriot on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Revere was the American rider of 1775; as a verb the word means to venerate.

clue.text: Pondered over type of carrier represented

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the pondering word lies across and around the carrier

parts.note: pored over a book means studied it intently
a tray is something used to carry dishes

explanation.surface: Someone studies a particular kind of carrier depicted in a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pondered over' looks like the set phrase 'pored over', but 'over' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray something is to depict or show it in art or words, which is what represented means here.

clue.text: He loved Pooh's friend, embracing the writer

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the friend goes round the writer

parts.note: Roo is the young kangaroo in Winnie-the-Pooh
the writer refers to the setter, me

explanation.surface: A setter recalls a beloved character from Winnie-the-Pooh giving him a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the writer' is the setter, a crossword convention. 'He loved' points to Shakespeare's lover of Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo is Shakespeare's archetypal lover, devoted to Juliet.

clue.text: French writer pinching university directory

indicators.note: pinching means gripping, so the writer's name holds the letter for university

parts.note: Andre Gide was a French Nobel prizewinning novelist

explanation.surface: A French author steals a university's list of contacts.
explanation.definitionFit: A guide is a handbook giving information, much like a directory of places or names.

clue.text: Man following extremely impassioned artistic style

indicators.note: following places the island after the extreme letters
extremely means taking the extreme letters, first and last, of the word

parts.note: IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man comes after an intensely passionate kind of art.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'impassioned' are I and D. 'Man' is the island in the Irish Sea, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom can mean a characteristic mode of expression in art or music, a distinctive style.

clue.text: Caretaker's solid figure guarding Channel Islands work unit

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding protectively, so the figure goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a cone is a solid geometric shape
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, such as Jersey and Guernsey
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A building's caretaker stands like a statue guarding a work unit in the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' suggests a person or a number; it is a geometric solid. The Channel Islands lie off Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A concierge is a porter or doorkeeper looking after an apartment block or hotel, a caretaker.

clue.text: Bill's companion? Goodness me!

definitions.meaning: in the phrase bill and ..., to whisper sweet nothings, it is the word paired with bill
an exclamation of surprise, chiefly British

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is from the phrase 'bill and coo', to whisper like lovebirds.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers bill and coo; also an exclamation of surprise, as in 'coo, look at that'.

clue.text: Draw game? He painted frescoes

parts.note: a draw in a match is a tie
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A drawn match prompts a question, and the answer is an artist known for murals.
explanation.walkthrough: Giambattista Tiepolo was an 18th-century Venetian painter famous for ceiling frescoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiepolo was the Venetian master of ceiling frescoes in palaces and churches across Europe.

clue.text: Instance of former member overcome by drink

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: overcome by means engulfed, so the member is swallowed by the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Here is a case of a former politician who has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome by drink' paints a drunk; it means the member sits inside the drink. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a single case representing a type, an instance.
